tools.name: describe_object
tools.title: Describe object
tools.description: Name, class, live check-in, recent code history (check-in ids, messages, times), data tables with columns and row counts, code file list, next alarm and preview state. Useful as the first call, to see what the object contains. target "preview" describes the preview copy (its schema, data counts and alarm).

tools.name: read_code
tools.title: Read code
tools.description: Files at a check-in: the live one by default, "preview" for the preview head, or a check-in id (prefix of 4+ characters works). Pass path for one file. Text comes back as strings; binary files as { base64 } when asked for by path, otherwise as a size stub. In the full listing, text files over 32 KiB come back as a size stub too; one file by path is returned up to 512 KiB.

tools.name: query_data
tools.title: Query data
tools.description: Read-only SQL over the object's own tables (SQLite dialect, see https://sqlite.org/lang_select.html). Reserved _perch_* tables and all writes are refused. target "preview" reads the preview copy. At most 500 rows.

tools.name: propose_change
tools.title: Propose change
tools.description: Change this object's code, static files and stored tests on a preview copy of the file; the live object is not touched until release_change. Takes whole files and exact-string edits, applies them to the preview (a copy of the live file, data included), builds it (the module graph loads and the constructor runs, which is where the code creates or changes its tables) and runs the stored tests. Code is TypeScript against the Cloudflare Durable Objects API (https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/api/). There is one pending change at a time: a later proposal adds to its files, and the preview's data is rebuilt from live every time, so calls made on the preview do not carry over. from_checkin starts from an earlier check-in's files, which is how code is rolled back; from_checkin "live" discards the pending change.

tools.name: read_object
tools.title: Read from object
tools.description: Read from this object without changing it: a GET or HEAD to the object's own fetch() handler or its public/ files, or a call to one of its public RPC methods (the routes and methods are the ones read_code shows). The runtime enforces the read: any SQL write, key-value write or alarm change made during the call is refused with an error and nothing is saved. target "preview" reads the preview copy. Use it to view pages and call getters.

tools.name: import_files
tools.title: Import static files
tools.description: Import a directory of static files (images, fonts, documents) from this machine's disk into the live object's public/ tree, as one check-in. The files stream from disk, so tens of thousands are fine and none pass through this conversation: give the directory path. Files already present with the same contents are skipped, so a repeat run is cheap. Changes the live object directly (static files cannot change what the class does); refused while a preview is unreleased. For code, tests and a few small files, use propose_change.

tools.name: release_change
tools.title: Release change
tools.description: Make the pending change live as one check-in, and start it on the live data (its constructor runs, applying any schema steps). Refused if the preview did not build, a stored test fails, or live moved since the preview was made. If the new code does not start on the live data, the release is undone and live keeps the code it had.

tools.name: call_object
tools.title: Call object
tools.description: Make a write call on this object: a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE to the object's own fetch() handler, or one of its public RPC methods (the routes and methods are the ones read_code shows). target "live" (the default) changes live data; target "preview" changes only the preview copy, and there kind "alarm" runs alarm() now (clearing the pending alarm unless the handler rescheduled it). Returns the result, console logs, rows written and the next alarm. For reads, use read_object.
